rows.description: A child sends smiling, crying or heart emoji and stickers to convey mood. Emoji stand in for tone and face but can be ambiguous, so the same emoji may mean different things to different people.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child sends voice notes or short videos to family and friends. Voice carries warmth and tone that text lacks, but recorded content can be forwarded, so children should think before sending.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A school-age child learns bhangra, Bharatanatyam, hip-hop or an instrument, and discovers that movement and sound can carry pride, longing or fun. Effort and repetition build both skill and confidence.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: playfulness, pride, nostalgia

rows.description: A child performing in a school play begins to notice laughter, silence or fidgeting and adjust. Audience reactions are cues about engagement, not a verdict on the child's worth.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child before a recital may show shaking hands or a dry voice, signs of nervous excitement as much as fear. Slow breathing, rehearsal and a familiar friendly face help the body settle.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: fear, anxiety, excitement, calm

rows.description: A school-age child builds a model, folds origami or makes a card, showing pride, patience and care for the recipient. Specific comments on the work support motivation better than general flattery.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child learns that a dove, a heart, a red cross or a flag stands for an idea, and that images can show mood through colour and composition. Symbols vary across cultures, so meaning must be checked.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A pre-teen wants a certain haircut or watch to fit in with classmates. Wanting to match peers is normal, and adults help by balancing family values, budget and the child's own taste.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child notices that a uniform, a house badge or matching gear signals membership and rules. Uniforms reduce visible difference, yet children still read shoes, bags and haircuts as status cues.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child stands, sings the anthem or lights a lamp in a morning assembly, following shared movements. Ritual gives shape to feeling, and some children need explanation before they find meaning in it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
